failures.criterion: A5 (R6): "A test sums the bytes of every .js response the browser fetches to open a fixture document that holds a view block, and the sum is at most 10,000 more than the base number the test pins."
failures.evidence: Reproduced independently at this head. `cd packages/dispatch && DATABASE_URL='postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5433/t_views?sslmode=disable' bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium e2e/view-budget.e2e.ts` fails the row `a view block costs the reader at most 10,000 more bytes of JavaScript`: `Error: A5: the document's JavaScript is 1791925 bytes against the base's 1778541`, `Expected: <= 1788541`, `Received: 1791925` — growth 13,384, which is 3,384 over the limit R6 and A5 set. The dependency half of A5 passes (both manifests' `dependencies` are byte-identical to the base). The limit is an approved acceptance value, so the change cannot be accepted against the spec as it stands; the architect has the question with the human at dispatch://INFRA-682/ask/fa4e3094-4deb-4bc9-afe5-84dfcfc0e203, which proposes 14,000. Nothing here is the implementer's to fix without that answer: this entry records the criterion as unmet, not as unproven.

failures.criterion: R6: "A page file is at most 5 MiB and a block's data at most 16 MiB." The block weighs the newest version of each data file, but sends the version the reference pins, so a reference to an over-limit old version passes the cap and is sent in full.
failures.evidence: New red test, `packages/dispatch/e2e/view-block.e2e.ts:1077`, `a view block counts the version it sends against 16 MiB, not the newest @phone`, committed as 6a4a3f1b5317. It uploads huge.json version 1 of 17 MiB and version 2 of 32 bytes, grants the file without a pin, and writes a block naming `…/artifact/huge-json@v1`. The block must show `data — the data files together are larger than 16 MiB, so Dispatch sends no data`. It shows no such line: `cd packages/dispatch && DATABASE_URL='postgres://legion_test@127.0.0.1:5433/t_views?sslmode=disable' bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts --project=chromium e2e/view-block.e2e.ts -g 'counts the version it sends'` gives `1 failed`, `Error: R6: the block weighs the version it sends, so a pinned 17 MiB version is over the limit … element(s) not found`. The same row fails in firefox in the full run. A throwaway probe over the same fixture recorded what actually happens: the browser fetched `/api/v1/artifacts/<huge id>/versions/1` and read 17,825,792 bytes, and the block's only paragraph was its caption — so the 17 MiB reaches the page through `postMessage`, which is the phone cost R6 bounds. The cause is one line: `resolveFile` (packages/dispatch/web/src/features/view/ViewBlock.tsx:129) returns `size: record.size ?? 0`, the latest version's size the summary carries, while it returns `version: pinned ?? latest`; `bytes += state.size` (:275) then weighs a version the block will not send. The converse is the same defect: a block pinned to a small old version of a file whose newest version is over 16 MiB is refused data it would have been right to send. A grant pinned to an old version takes the same path. The existing 16 MiB row (:1038) cannot catch either, because it names only the newest version. The fix is the pinned version's own size; the summary carries only the latest version's, so it needs either a size per version in the summary read or a HEAD of the pinned version before the cap is applied — a design choice for the implementer, within the "one summary read and one read of the new version's bytes" budget departure D1 already weighed.
